doc.about.title: About Ask Canada
doc.about.lede: A plain-language front door to every federal service, built on official sources.
doc.about.body:
## What this is
Ask Canada helps you find and understand Government of Canada services. Ask a question in your own words, in English or French, and get a short answer with a link to the exact official page it came from. When a question needs more than words, Ask Canada adds a tool to the conversation: a planner, a calculator, a checklist or live data.

## What it isn’t
Ask Canada is an independent service. It is not the Government of Canada and does not speak for any department. It never signs you in, submits applications or takes payments. When it’s time to do that, it sends you to the official site.

## Where answers come from
Answers are drawn from official pages on canada.ca and other Government of Canada sites, and from public data such as weather alerts, travel advisories, recalls and statutory holidays. Every fee, date and deadline shows when it was last checked. Always confirm on the linked official page before you act.

## Open and adoptable
Ask Canada is built to Government of Canada web standards: official languages, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), privacy by design and strict security. It is designed so a government team could adopt and run it.
doc.privacy.title: Privacy notice
doc.privacy.lede: Private by design, not by policy. Here is exactly what happens to what you ask.
doc.privacy.body:
## What we don’t collect
No account, no name, no email. We don’t use tracking cookies, analytics profiles or advertising. We never ask for your Social Insurance Number, passport number, banking details or passwords, and you should never type them here.

## Your questions
When you ask a question, it is sent to our server to write the answer, then it is not kept. Conversations are not stored on our servers or used to build profiles. If an AI model provider processes the question, it is sent without your identity and under terms that don’t allow it to be used for training.

## What stays on your device
Recent chats, plans, checklists and reminders you save are kept in your browser’s local storage, on this device only. They never leave it. You can remove them any time with “Clear this device” in the Menu or the footer.

## Abuse protection
To keep the service available, we count requests per network address for a few minutes to stop automated abuse. We keep only a scrambled (hashed) form of the address, in memory, and never log it. An invisible bot check also runs when you send a question: in the background, your browser answers a short technical challenge from our hosting provider (Vercel BotID), so automated scripts can’t use up the service. There is no puzzle to solve. The check looks at technical signals from your browser, not at what you ask, and we don’t use it to identify you, build a profile or follow you across sites.

## Official sites
When you continue to canada.ca or another official site, that site’s own privacy notice applies.
doc.accessibility.title: Accessibility
doc.accessibility.lede: Everyone should be able to use government services. Here is how we build for that.
doc.accessibility.body:
## Our standard
Ask Canada aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 level AA, the standard referenced by the Government of Canada’s Standard on Web Accessibility and EN 301 549.

## What we do
- Every control works with a keyboard, with a visible focus ring. Press “/” to jump to the question box and Esc to stop an answer.
- Answers are announced to screen readers as they finish, and every tool has a text alternative.
- Colours meet contrast requirements in light and dark mode, and motion is reduced when your device asks for it.
- You can ask by voice, have answers read aloud, and use the site at any zoom level without sideways scrolling.
- English and French have full, reviewed interfaces. Answers are also available in many other languages.

## Known limitations
- Menus in languages other than English and French use English until native speakers review them.
- Maps are paired with a text list, but map panning is easier with a mouse or touch.
doc.terms.title: Terms of use
doc.terms.lede: Plain terms for a plain-language service.
doc.terms.body:
## Information, not advice
Ask Canada gives general information based on official sources. It isn’t legal, financial or medical advice, and it can make mistakes. Always confirm on the linked official page before you apply, pay or make a decision.

## Independent service
Ask Canada is not the Government of Canada. Program names and information belong to their departments. Official decisions are made only by the responsible department.

## Use it fairly
Don’t use the service to harm others, commit fraud, or overload it with automated requests. We may limit requests to keep it available for everyone.

## Emergencies
Ask Canada is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 911. In a suicide or mental health crisis, call or text 9-8-8, any time.
